turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: I will not be denied, I insist that you play with me, now.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid I don't know how to play the games you have here, ma'am.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy, you will learn, I will teach you.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: But it's not that, ma'am, it's just that I'm not used to such grand things.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: I care not for your humble beginnings, I want you to play with me.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid I'll get in trouble with my sister if I stay too long, ma'am.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: I will speak to your sister, she will be delighted to hear that you are staying with me.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: No, ma'am, it's not that, it's just that I have a lot of work to do at home.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: I will not be put off, I demand that you play with me.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm sorry, ma'am, but I really must go.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Estella, where are you? Come and take this boy away.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm sorry to leave without finishing our conversation, ma'am.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will not leave until you have played with me, I have not been forgotten for nothing.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid I'm not very good company, ma'am.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: I do not want good company, I want someone to play with, to dance with.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I don't know how to dance, ma'am.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: I will teach you, I will show you how to dance like a gentleman.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid I'm not very good at it, ma'am.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: We will see about that, I will not be disappointed.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Thank you, ma'am, for your kindness.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Come nearer; let me look at you. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Look at me. You are not afraid of a woman who has never seen the sun since you were born?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Do you know what I touch here?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I am tired. I want diversion, and I have done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I sometimes have sick fancies, and I have a sick fancy that I want to see some play. There, there!

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: No, ma’am, I am very sorry for you, and very sorry I can’t play just now. If you complain of me I shall get into trouble with my sister, so I would do it if I could; but it’s so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.
